screening_decisions.reason: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover trial of systemic inosiplex in alopecia totalis. Meets RCT and intervention criteria.
Placebo-controlled trial; patients randomly divided into oral prednisolone pulse therapy vs placebo for extensive AA. RCT of systemic intervention.
Multicenter, prospective, randomized, controlled trial comparing topical betamethasone valerate foam vs lotion in AA. RCT of topical intervention.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled study of topical minoxidil in extensive AA; design implies randomisation (half-scalp allocation). Conservative include as potential RCT.
Double-blind trial assigning patients to topical minoxidil or placebo; unclear if randomized but controlled trial of intervention for AA. Include due to uncertainty.
Randomized double-blind design evaluating topical DPCP +/- minoxidil for chronic severe AA. RCT of topical interventions.
Patients randomly assigned to topical cyclosporine, PUVA, or IV thymopentin for AA totalis/universalis. RCT of topical and systemic interventions.
Only 6 patients, no control group, no randomisation described; not a randomized controlled trial (split-scalp application not stated as randomized).
Patients randomized to topical cyclosporine A vs vehicle in AA. RCT of topical intervention.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled study of systemic imipramine in AA. Likely an RCT; include conservatively.
Patients randomly assigned to topical immunotherapy, systemic interferon, or both for severe AA. RCT of topical and systemic interventions.
Double-blind study of topical cyclosporin A vs placebo in AA. No explicit randomisation, but controlled trial design; include conservatively.
Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of clobetasol foam in moderate to severe AA. RCT of topical intervention.
Randomized, controlled trial of systemic prednisone +/- topical minoxidil in AA. RCT of systemic and topical interventions.
Not a single RCT; describes a series of studies and long-term follow-up, lacks a clear controlled trial design for this report. Exclude as non-primary trial.
Controlled trial comparing therapies vs placebo in patchy AA. Abstract does not explicitly state randomisation, but controlled design suggests likely RCT; include conservatively.
Questionnaire study on patient perceptions of AA; not a randomised controlled trial evaluating an intervention.
Methodological discussion on when RCTs are unnecessary; not a trial itself.
Randomized, double-blind, controlled trial of aromatherapy (essential oils) in AA. RCT of a topical intervention.
Review/update article on alopecia areata; not a primary randomised controlled trial.
Incidence study in a community population; not an intervention trial.
Prognostic factor study among patients treated with diphenylcyclopropenone; not a randomised controlled trial.
Subjects divided into matched groups (age/sex), not randomly assigned; a non-randomised controlled study.
Review article on genetics of AA; not a trial.
Article discussing quality assessment of clinical trials; not a trial itself.
